title: Embeddings bucketization and macro-tier ideas
content:
Personal scratchpad — thinking about simpler pricing for embeddings + bundling strategy

Goal: make embeddings predictable and cheap for common vector workloads while preserving unit-econ for high-density customers (search indexes, semantic stores). Keep product friction low (no micro-metering surprises).

High-level ideas (rough):
- Bucketization: round up embedding requests into vector buckets (e.g., 1-8, 9-32, 33-128, 129-512). Charge per-bucket rather than per-vector to reduce billing noise and encourage packs.
- Macro tiers: offer three embedding-focused SKUs: "Starter Vectors" (low volume, latency-friendly), "Index Builder" (medium volume, batching/async), "Enterprise Vectorpool" (committed capacity, private placements, higher throughput + KMS).
- Credits & bundles: convert monthly commit into vector-credits, usable for inference+indexing. Bundles give 10–30% discount over pay-as-you-go. Bursts beyond commit consume credits at a premium.

Assumptions to sanity-check (back-of-envelope):
- Model/embedding compute: 1 GPU-hour builds roughly N embeddings depending on model and batch size. For ballpark: a mid-sized GPU (A100 equiv) can encode ~200k vectors/hr at batch sizes tuned (embedding dim 1536) — ambiguous, needs perf test.
- Cost numbers (placeholders): host compute cost = $4/hr GPU-equivalent (amortized infra + infra ops). If 200k vectors/hr -> compute cost per 1k vectors ≈ $0.02. Add storage+I/O+indexing overhead ~ $0.01–0.03/1k vectors => raw unit cost ~ $0.03–0.05 / 1k vectors.
- Target gross margin: 60–75% for hosted. So list price target per 1k vectors = $0.08–0.2 depending on tier and latency.

Bucket pricing sketch (illustrative):
- 1-8 vectors -> price 1 credit (min bucket) = $0.002/request or equivalent of 8 vectors priced at per-1k = heavy premium (good for single-shot embedding in UI flows).
- 9-32 vectors -> price 3 credits (~$0.006)
- 33-128 vectors -> price 9 credits (~$0.018)
- 129-512 vectors -> price 28 credits (~$0.056)
Rationale: encourage batching (per-vector price falls fast as you move up). Also easier for front-end devs: they can pack calls into a single request to reduce cost.

Macro tiers (sketch):
- Starter Vectors: payg price, per-bucket pricing above, 0.5M vectors/mo typical. No commits, realtime SLA best-effort. Good for prototypes.
- Index Builder: monthly commit (e.g., $Xk/mo) gives ~20% discount. Includes async bulk embedding pipeline + priority background batch windows. For teams creating/updating large indexes frequently.
- Enterprise Vectorpool: reserved capacity -> dedicated pools for embedding ops (private networking option), guaranteed throughput SLO, custom quantization/throughput tradeoffs, volume & latency SLAs. Price: negotiated, but baseline commit => big discount + access to index-building appliances.

Examples (very rough math):
Scenario A: startup with 200k documents, vector dim 1536, 1 embedding per doc (reindex nightly). -> 200k embeddings/week -> ~800k/mo. At $0.10/1k vectors => $80/mo. If commit tier gives 20% off -> $64/mo. If they batch and fit into 33-128 buckets pricing, effective cost drops further.

Scenario B: search service with heavy read traffic but small writes: 10k new vectors/day -> 300k/mo. Monthly cost at $0.10/1k = $30/mo (starter). But embedding compute amortization might be larger if small docs cause low batch efficiency — indicator to promote "index builder" tier offering big-batch reindex windows.

Unit-econ knobs to iterate on:
- Bucket cut points and multipliers (how to design bins so common SDK patterns align, e.g., single-sentence, multi-sentence arrays, batch indexing).
- Min-charge per request to avoid tiny vector spam.
- Commit vs payg discount curves and burst-overage premium.
- Pricing for synchronous low-latency vs async bulk (lower price for async).
- Storage/indexing charges separate? Pros: clarity. Cons: more complexity. Probably keep compact: combine embedding compute+indexing into single vector-credit for most customers, separate for enterprise.

Operational considerations:
- Metering: easiest is to meter at the API gateway (count vectors in request body post-aggregation). Need to ensure SDKs don't hide batching semantics. Document best practices (pack requests).
- Billing UX: show estimated per-request price in Console playground. Visualize how batching reduces cost.
- Abuse: small vectors used to probe free tiers -> enforce min-charge and rate limits.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Perf validation: run embedding throughput microbenchmarks for our most-used models (Ada-like, medium open models, and a LLM-based encoder) to validate the 200k/hr assumption. Jira PRIC-342 assigned.
- What is typical vector size distribution for customers (1–8, 9–32, >32)? Need telemetry from SDKs / logs (privacy-safe).
- How to price similarity search vs just storing? Charge for creation and cheap reads? Or meter both?
- How does Dedicated/Private change unit-econ? For Dedicated, we can offer lower per-vector price assuming committed utilization of GPUs; need decommit modeling.
- Edge-case: embeddings with heavy pre/post-processing (multi-model pipelines). Bill composite flow either as sum of ops or as packaged "pipeline credit". Prefer packaging for UX simplicity.

Quick action items:
- Spike: bench embeddings throughput on dev cluster (Ethan + infra). Capture vectors/hr at batch sizes [1,8,32,128] for model A and B.
- Product: prototype bucketizer on API gateway and simulate billing impacts with sampled request shapes (Ava).
- Finance: run sensitivity analysis on margin vs per-1k price and commit discount (Priya + finance).

Notes to self: keep product friction low. If we create too many micro-buckets, everyone will be confused. 4 buckets looks like a good starting point. Emphasize SDK patterns for batching and show cost wins in Console.

Rough mental target prices (placeholders to iterate):
- PAYG per-1k vectors: $0.10 (Starter)
- Index builder commit price per-1k: $0.07 (20–30% off)
- Enterprise reserved: $0.03–0.06 per-1k depending on commit size & private infra

Random scribbles:
- Could experiment with token-equivalent packaging: e.g., 1 vector credit = cost-equivalent of N tokens for parity with chat/embedding economics. Might make cross-product bundling easier.
- Consider "index-incremental" credits: cheaper for delta updates (only new vectors) and more expensive for full reindex. Encourage incremental flows.
- Bundling idea: include Xk vector credits with token credits in some product SKUs (useful for RAG products).

End of scratchpad. Will formalize into a short PRD once perf numbers come back.
